text:
ops-bot: ALERT: regression detected — p99 latency for model spectrax-v1 in us-west-2 increased 3.1x over the last 15m. routing: hosted, tier: standard

sophie: seeing this on support tickets too. multiple customers hitting long-doc endpoints time out around 15s. p95 up ~2x.

maria: thanks — which rollout was this? we onboarded spectrax-v1 yesterday with tokenizer-normalize=v2.

kevin: confirmed rollout. we also pushed a runtime kernel tweak for packing at 02:10 UTC. suspect interaction between tokenizer-normalize=v2 and kvcache keying.

raj: logs look like KV cache misses spike whenever requests include >16k tokens. cache regen attempts are frequent: 
```
[2026-03-17T02:14:05Z] kvcache: key_mismatch: sha1(prefix_norm) != stored_key, regen triggered
[2026-03-17T02:14:06Z] kvcache: regen_success duration=82ms size=24MB
[2026-03-17T02:14:06Z] kvcache: eviction thrash count=87
```

sophie: customers show similar payloads but older models stable. suggests model-specific tokenizer change is the delta.

kevin: quick repro I ran: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"spectrax-v1","input":"<16k tokens of doc>...","stream":false}'
```
p95 locally jumped from 120ms -> 560ms when using tokenizer-normalize=v2 keys.

maria: any customer-facing mitigation we can deploy fast?

raj: short term: route long-context traffic for spectrax-v1 to spectrax-v1-smallcache (variant without normalize=v2) — that's a config flip in routing. reduces cache key mismatches.

lucas: rolled out route override to canary for 10% of traffic in us-west-2. need to monitor error/latency.

ops-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: route_override applied to spectrax-v1 -> spectrax-v1-smallcache (canary=10%) by lucas at 2026-03-17T02:23:44Z

kevin: also pushed an immediate guard in runtime: if kvcache regen rate > 30/min, switch to soft-prefix-caching to avoid eviction thrash. can be toggled without deploy via /runtime/flags.

raj: toggled soft-prefix-caching flag for us-west-2. watching p95/p99.

sophie: support note: templating replies to affected customers with "temporary routing change" + request example to help us reproduce.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: tokenizer-normalize=v2 changes subword normalization for certain unicode sequences. kvcache key computation uses post-tokenization prefix fingerprint, but our preprocessor used a slightly different normalization path for cached keys. mismatch only appears for long prefix boundaries; short contexts unaffected.

maria: plan: 1) keep canary routing + soft-prefix-caching; 2) add deterministic normalization path in runtime to align keys; 3) coordinate tokenizer rollback if needed. target timeline: patch normalization in 12h, full rollout 24-36h.

raj: repro steps for engineers: 
1) use payload with repeated multi-byte sequences (e.g., CJK + emoji + combining marks) ~12k-18k tokens
2) call spectrax-v1 and check kvcache logs for key_mismatch entries
3) toggle runtime flag `kvcache.soft_prefix=true` and confirm miss rate drops

kevin: quick mitigation note — enabling `kvcache.soft_prefix` reduces p99 by ~40% in my canary runs, but increases some token compute (more re-generation) so watch cost.

maria: customer comms drafted, tagging legal for any SLO credit discussion for impacted customers.

lucas: after toggles, us-west-2 p99 dropped to 1.3x baseline, p95 near baseline. continuing to monitor for 1h before wider routing change.

sophie: closing loop: will update each ticket with "we're investigating; temporary routing applied; next update in 1h"

ops-bot: ALERT-RESOLVE: p99 for spectrax-v1 reduced to 1.2x at 2026-03-17T02:44:10Z (post-mitigation)

kevin: follow-ups: add deterministic normalization unit tests, add a fuzz test around the tokenizer + kvcache key pipeline, and schedule full normalization patch rollout tomorrow morning.

maria: assigning follow-up tickets to eng-runtime (KEVIN) and eng-ml (TOKENIZER TEAM) — will sync in 2h.

sophie: thanks all. keeping this thread open while we watch metrics. :thumbsup:
